entities.summary: Thomas Cole was an Anglo-American artist who founded the Hudson River School art movement. He painted romantic landscapes and history paintings. Influenced by European painters, but with a strong American sensibility, he was prolific throughout his career and worked primarily with oil on canvas. His paintings are typically allegoric and often depict small figures or structures set against moody and evocative natural landscapes. They are usually escapist, framing the New World as a natural eden contrasting with the smog-filled cityscapes of Industrial Revolution-era Britain, in which he grew up.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a founder of the Hudson River School, Thomas Cole's landscapes influenced American art and shaped the nation's perception of its natural environment. His works also contributed to the development of the American Romantic movement.
